reading.body:
QTS Santa Clara 1 in Santa Clara, California, publishes 7.5 MW of IT capacity, operated by Quality Technology Services.

At 10 kW per rack, a common enterprise colocation density, that load supports roughly 750 racks. At 40 kW per rack, a density closer to AI training workloads, it supports roughly 188 racks. The operator has not published a per-rack power envelope, so neither figure is the operator's own claim, only what the published megawattage implies under each assumption.

QTS Santa Clara 1 holds 1 published certification: LEED (a specific compliance or security standard). Together these qualify the facility for regulated workloads spanning security auditing, payments, and healthcare data, though which specific tenants rely on which certification is not disclosed.

California has 22 facilities mapped in this site's dataset, of which 10 publish a megawatt figure, totaling 356 MW. QTS Santa Clara 1 contributes 7.5 MW of that total. At that published size it is a small facility relative to what frontier AI training infrastructure requires, which now runs into the tens or hundreds of megawatts, though it may still support inference workloads or smaller-scale AI applications.
